newsitem.title: USA: GM's Oldsmobile sales down 14 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: GM's Oldsmobile sales down 14 pct in 1996.

text.p: Sales at General Motors Corp's Oldsmobile division fell 14 percent in 1996 to about 330,000 vehicles, the automaker said on Friday.
Oldsmobile said it was aiming to boost sales this year as new models became available.

Bill Farmer, general sales manager at Oldsmobile, said retail sales, which exclude sales to daily rental car companies and other large fleet operators, dropped 14 percent last year to around 240,000 vehicles.

Farmer said Oldsmobile aimed to increase retail sales by 10 percent in 1997 while reducing non-profitable fleet sales to rental car firms. Part of the increase will come from sales of the new Oldsmobile Silhouette minivan, as well as the Cutlass and Intrigue models, he said.
Oldsmobile officials told reporters at the Los Angeles Auto Show that the Intrigue begins production this quarter and should be available in the second quarter.
Farmer said production of the Silhouette, part of a new line of GM minivans, should reach full speed this spring.
